facts.text: Collision timestamp from Vehicle A ECU power contactor / cascading error messages: 16:36:12.7 EDT on May 7, 2016 (t = 10.43 s after cresting hill at 345 m / 33.08 m/s).
facts.citation: docket_har1702.txt p.15, p.29; docket_tech_recon_factual.txt p.12; facts.md F1, F28

facts.text: Vehicle A (2015 sedan) traveling eastbound at constant 74 mph (33.08 m/s) with Traffic-Aware Cruise Control (TACC) set to 74 mph 1 min 51 s before impact and Autosteer active.
facts.citation: docket_har1702.txt p.11, p.13, p.15; docket_tech_recon_factual.txt p.12

facts.text: Posted speed limit on US-27A at crash location is 65 mph (29.06 m/s); design speed 70 mph; 85th percentile speed 69 mph.
facts.citation: docket_har1702.txt p.11, p.22; docket_highway_att5_spot_speed.txt p.2

facts.text: Vertical hill crest on eastbound US-27A is 1,132 ft (345.0 m) west of the NE 140th Court intersection, with a 2.15% descending grade for 1,459 ft (444.7 m).
facts.citation: docket_har1702.txt p.22, p.29; docket_tech_recon_factual.txt p.3; docket_highway_factual.txt p.10

facts.text: At 74 mph over the 1,132 ft (345 m) sight distance from the vertical crest, both drivers had up to 10.4 seconds of unobstructed line of sight.
facts.citation: docket_har1702.txt p.29; docket_vehicle_dynamics_study.txt p.1-2

facts.text: US-27A has four 12-ft (3.66 m) through travel lanes (two eastbound, two westbound), with 2-ft (0.61 m) inside shoulders and 5-ft (1.52 m) outside paved shoulders.
facts.citation: docket_har1702.txt p.13, p.21; docket_highway_factual.txt p.9

facts.text: US-27A grass median is ~60 ft (18.29 m) wide; total separation including left-turn lane and shoulders is 78 ft (23.77 m), with a 130 ft (39.6 m) paved median crossover.
facts.citation: docket_har1702.txt p.13, p.21, p.29 fn.53; docket_tech_recon_factual.txt p.3-4

facts.text: Left-turn lanes on US-27A extend approximately 550 ft (167.6 m; measured 557 ft WB and 528 ft EB) in advance of the intersection.
facts.citation: docket_har1702.txt p.13; docket_tech_recon_factual.txt p.4; docket_highway_factual.txt p.9

facts.text: Overall length of the 2014 truck-tractor and 2003 53-ft semitrailer combination was 71 ft 7 in (21.82 m); impact was centered 45 ft 5 in (13.84 m) rearward of the tractor front.
facts.citation: docket_har1702.txt p.6 fn.6; docket_tech_recon_factual.txt p.10-11

facts.text: No pre-collision braking or evasive steering roadway marks were found for either vehicle; a 11.5 ft (3.51 m) vertical-loading tire friction mark was documented at the POI.
facts.citation: docket_har1702.txt p.15, p.28; docket_tech_recon_factual.txt p.4-5 Fig. 1

facts.text: After passing beneath the semitrailer, Vehicle A traveled at a 1.7 deg angle to the right, departing the paved roadway ~326 ft (99.4 m) east of the POI.
facts.citation: docket_crash_summary.txt p.2; docket_tech_recon_factual.txt p.4

facts.text: Vehicle A airbags deployed at 16:36:21.1 EDT (8.4 seconds after initial impact with the semitrailer) when it struck and severed the utility pole at 49.05 mph (21.93 m/s).
facts.citation: docket_har1702.txt p.15; docket_tech_recon_factual.txt p.13

facts.text: Vehicle A traveled a total linear distance of 910 ft (277.4 m) from the POI, coming to rest 55 ft (16.8 m) east of the severed utility pole, facing north.
facts.citation: docket_har1702.txt p.11, p.13 Fig. 2; docket_tech_recon_factual.txt p.4-5

facts.text: Witness A was driving westbound in the outside lane at ~60 mph (26.82 m/s) about 0.25 mi (402 m) east of the truck, seeing Vehicle A crest the hill for 2-3 s (including t=4.0 s at X=337.7 m) before the turning semitrailer blocked his view.
facts.citation: docket_har1702.txt p.11-12, p.29-30; docket_vehicle_dynamics_study.txt p.4, p.8; witness_A.md p.1

facts.text: Witness B testified she stood "out front of the store" with an unobstructed view of Vehicle A all the way to impact, but her pen mark #2 on Exhibit 4 (Depo Witness B 1:54:34) places her at [8.5, 0, 9.0] m — directly behind the bench shelter (centered at [8.5, 8.2] m with an opaque sheet-metal back) and behind the path of the turning tractor-semitrailer at t=9.9 s.
facts.citation: Depo Witness B 41:10-41:20, 52:00-52:07, 1:54:34 (Exhibit 4 mark #2); Depo Witness D 10:16-10:29; exhibit4_intersection_map.png

facts.text: Witness C was stopped in a pickup in the westbound inside lane of US-27A at [-18.0, 0, -31.09] m (18 m west of the NE 140th Ct crossover).
facts.citation: witness_C.md p.1; police_report.md p.1

facts.text: Witness D (store counter clerk) was inside the retail store behind the register at [24.0, 0, 15.0] m; the drink cooler and window posters blocked any view of the highway.

extraction.notes:
KEY DISCREPANCIES & REVIEWER NOTES:
1. Witness B Marked Position vs. Bench Shelter Occlusion (Depo Witness B vs. Exhibit 4 & Depo Witness D): In her deposition, Witness B repeatedly testifies that she stood 'out front of the store' and had an uninterrupted, clear view of the eastbound car from the moment it crested the hill until impact, with 'nothing in the way' (Depo Witness B 41:10, 52:00, 56:15). However, when asked to mark her standing position on Exhibit 4 (Depo Witness B 1:54:30, Mark #2), she places her mark at approximately [9.0, 12.6] m — directly behind (south-southeast of) the 'bench shelter (open sides)' drawn on Exhibit 4 at [7.5..10.6, 8.9..11.2] m. In Video 2, Witness D (the store clerk) testifies that this bench shelter has a roof on posts and a solid sheet-metal back (Depo Witness D 09:51, 10:16) and that she told Witness B she could wait at the bench (Depo Witness D 30:40). From [9.0, 12.6] m looking north-northwest toward the point of impact [0, 0] and the approach lane just west of the intersection, the bench shelter sits directly in the line of sight.
2. Witness D's Testimony Regarding Witness B: Witness D confirms she was inside behind the counter with windows covered by posters and a drink cooler (Depo Witness D 06:39, 08:08) and did not see the crash or where Witness B was standing at the moment of impact (Depo Witness D 42:35, 42:47). Witness D only saw Witness B outside after taking ~10-15 seconds to walk out the front door after the bang (Depo Witness D 19:09, 24:24), at which time Witness B stated she had 'a clear view of the car the whole way in' (Depo Witness D 31:20).
3. Eye Heights (Inferred vs. Cited): Truck driver eye height of 7.6 ft (2.32 m) and car driver eye height of 3.5 ft (1.07 m) are cited from AASHTO guidelines in docket_tech_recon_factual.txt p.17 and docket_har1702.txt p.39 fn.50. Witness B testifies she is 5'6" (1.68 m) tall and was standing (Depo Witness B 17:01, 22:57, 1:54:12), giving an inferred standing eye height of ~1.56 m (or 1.6 m standard standing adult). Eye heights for Witness A (~1.5 m seated in a Ram pickup), Witness C (~1.5 m seated in a pickup), and Witness D (1.6 m standing adult) are inferred from vehicle/posture types as they are not explicitly stated in the text.
4. Preliminary vs. Final NTSB Report Values: docket_preliminary_report.txt p.1 (and FL Traffic Crash Report p.2) lists the crash time as ~4:40 p.m., median width as 75 ft, median opening as 132 ft, impact at 23 ft forward of trailer end, and post-impact travel to the pole as 297 ft plus 50 ft to rest. The final adopted board report (docket_har1702.txt / facts.md) and Technical Reconstruction Factual Report supersede these with: impact time 4:36:12.7 p.m. EDT, median width ~60 ft, median opening 129-130 ft, impact contact 23.91-28.58 ft forward of trailer rear (centered 45 ft 5 in behind tractor front), and total post-impact travel of 910 ft (departing roadway at 326 ft, 334 ft through culvert/fence, 195 ft to pole, and 55 ft to final rest).
5. Road Skew and Orientation: In the real world, US-27A is oriented at ~288°/108° (WNW-ESE) and NE 140th Court intersects at a 109° angle (docket_tech_recon_factual.txt p.3). In Exhibit 4 (exhibit4_intersection_map.png) and facts.md p.2, the road is schematically straightened to run due East-West (+X) with NE 140th Court running due South (+Z) at 90°. Note also that FHP Motor Carrier Inspection (docket_vehicle_att3_fhp_inspection.txt p.5) erroneously refers to US-27 as 'North bound' and NE 140th Ave as 'West'.

findings.summary: Witness B's pen mark #2 on Exhibit 4 places her at [8.5, 0, 9.0] m (immediately against the south back of the bench shelter), where both the bench shelter and the turning tractor-semitrailer block her claimed continuous view of Vehicle A right up until impact.
findings.detail: In her deposition, Witness B testified that she stood outside in front of the store and had 'a clear view of the car the whole way in. I watched it right up until the moment it hit. Nothing was in the way' (Depo Witness B 41:10-41:20, 52:00-52:07, 56:00-56:18). However, when asked to mark her exact standing position on Exhibit 4 (Depo Witness B 1:54:24-1:54:50; frame at 1:54:34), the center of her red circled-X pen mark (#2) falls directly on the south edge of the bench shelter rectangle (which spans X = 6.75..10.25 m, Z = 7.45..8.95 m, centered at [8.5, 8.2] m per Exhibit 4's 40 m scale bar and AOI origin [0, 0]). Measured with Exhibit 4's scale bar (8.025 px/m), her mark #2 is at [8.5, 0, 9.0] m—not [7.5, 0, 12.0] m as coded in Round 3. Furthermore, her claim 'watched it right up until the moment it hit' requires evaluating her sightline in the last second before the t=10.43s impact (t=9.9s, as shown in overhead_t9p9.png), not at t=9.5s before the truck's cab and trailer interpose. From [8.5, 0, 9.0] m, the sheet-metal back of the bench shelter (Depo Witness D 10:16-10:29) and the turning tractor-semitrailer (veh_truck_tractor and veh_semitrailer) cross directly between Witness B and Vehicle A during the final second before impact (t ≈ 9.6s to 10.43s), making her claim physically impossible. The world module is patched to place Witness B at [8.5, 0, 9.0] m with observationTime = 9.9 s.

evidence.citation: Scale bar 0-40 m and AOI reference at [0,0]; bench shelter centered at [8.5, 8.2] m; pen mark #2 centered at [8.5, 9.0] m

findings.summary: Driving witnesses A and C were modeled with static eye coordinates rather than riding with their vehicles (`vehicleId` and `driverEye` pose updates in `setTime`), and Witness A's observationTime was set to t=7.0s (when the tractor already blocked his view) instead of during his clear-view window before the trailer entered the eastbound lanes.
findings.detail: Witness A was driving a black pickup truck westbound at ~60 mph (~0.25 mi behind the tractor-trailer) and testified that he saw Vehicle A crest the hill and descend for 2–3 seconds before the turning semitrailer entered the eastbound lanes and blocked his view (docket_har1702.txt p.11-12, p.29-30; docket_hp_att4_witness_interview.txt p.5-6, p.12, p.24-25; witness_A.md p.1). In the Round 3 world module, Witness A's eye position was fixed at [257.26, 0, -34.75] without `vehicleId: 'veh_witness_a_pickup'` or dynamic updates in `setTime(t)`, and his `observationTime` was set to t=7.0s, where the independent check showed `veh_truck_tractor` already blocking the ray to `veh_car_a` as the truck crossed the median. Similarly, Witness C (stopped in his pickup at [-18.0, 0, -31.09] m) lacked `vehicleId: 'veh_witness_c_pickup'` and dynamic `driverEye` updates in `setTime(t)`. In the patched world, both witnesses are bound to their vehicles via `vehicleId` and updated in `setTime(t)` from `vehicle.userData.driverEye`, and Witness A's `observationTime` is set to t=4.0s (during the 2–3 s window after Vehicle A crests the hill and before Vehicle T's turn blocks his sightline, consistent with docket_vehicle_dynamics_study.txt p.8 Table 2).

findings.summary: Roadway geometry, vertical crest profile, vehicle speeds, impact alignment, and post-impact trajectory match the NTSB factual reports and crash reconstruction.
findings.detail: US-27A is modeled with four 12-ft (3.66 m) lanes, a 78-ft (23.77 m) median/turn-lane separation, a 130-ft (39.6 m) crossover, and a vertical crest 1,132 ft (345.0 m) west of the intersection descending at 2.15% (docket_har1702.txt p.13, p.21-22, p.29; docket_tech_recon_factual.txt p.3-4). Vehicle A approaches eastbound at a constant 74 mph (33.08 m/s) with no pre-impact braking skids, striking the right side of the 53-ft semitrailer 45 ft 5 in (13.84 m) behind the tractor front at t=10.43s, then departing the right roadside at ~1.7° (326 ft / 99.4 m), breaching two wire fences, severing the utility pole at 855 ft (260.6 m) at t=18.83s (8.4 s after impact), and coming to rest at 910 ft (277.4 m) (docket_har1702.txt p.11, p.15-16; docket_tech_recon_factual.txt p.4-5, p.12-13). All independent plausibility and timing checks pass.

evidence.citation: plausibility veh_car_a, veh_truck_tractor, veh_semitrailer, veh_witness_a_pickup: pass; timing veh_car_a→veh_semitrailer: availableS 10.43s (sufficient)

findings.summary: Scene lighting, clear weather, dry pavement, sun position (azimuth 265.0°, elevation 45.1°), and absence of glare or active headlights match the documentary record and solar audit; no real scene footage exists.
findings.detail: The crash occurred on May 7, 2016 at 16:36:12.7 EDT (UTC-04:00) at 29.4106° N, -82.53979° W in clear daylight with dry roads (docket_har1702.txt p.11, p.15, p.32 fn.40; docket_tech_recon_factual.txt p.16; police_report.md p.1). The NOAA solar calculation and the NTSB Technical Reconstruction Group Factual Report (p.16: sun azimuth 264.2°–265.6°, elevation 46.4°–44.2°) match the rendered sun at azimuth 265.0° and elevation 45.1° (0.0° error; shadow bearing 85° E). Vehicle A's headlights are off in accordance with the downloaded ECU data (docket_driver_assistance_factual.txt p.7-8; docket_har1702.txt p.15). No witness or driver has `glareRisk: true`; the smallest sun-to-sight-line angle for any witness is 45.2° (`wit_witness_A`), and the smallest sun-to-travel-direction angle for any driver is 45.1° (`veh_witness_a_pickup`), consistent with Witness A's and Witness B's testimony that the sun was high and not in their eyes (docket_har1702.txt p.12, p.30; Depo Witness B 23:44-24:01, 34:19-34:27). No real scene footage exists to compare lighting against; lighting was compared against the documentary record and computed sun position only.

results.subject: veh_car_a
results.detail: The driver of Vehicle A: 2015 4-door passenger sedan had a continuous line of sight to Vehicle T (Semitrailer): 2003 53-ft white refrigerated van semitrailer for 10.43 s before impact (t=0.00–10.43 s), from the start of the reconstructed timeline, so this is a lower bound. Typical perception-reaction time is 1.5 s (range 1–2.5 s). Time available is more than the 2.5 s upper bound, so there was time to perceive and begin reacting. Vehicle T (Semitrailer): 2003 53-ft white refrigerated van semitrailer came within 3 m of the centerline of this driver's remaining path 1.73 s before impact. Kinematic estimate from the reconstructed geometry; it does not account for attention, conspicuity, glare or expectation.
